questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code starts and stops its worker goroutines? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Submit() is called when all queue slots are occupied and every worker is busy. What happens?
choices: It returns ErrQueueFull immediately, pushing the decision about retrying or shedding to the caller
The caller blocks until a slot frees up
The oldest queued request is dropped to make room
A new worker goroutine is started

questions.prompt: Shutdown() closes jobs while the queue still holds requests. What happens to those requests?
choices: They are discarded because the channel is closed
They are returned to callers as ErrClosed
Workers continue ranging over the closed channel until it is drained, so they are still processed before the workers exit
They are processed only if Submit is called again

questions.prompt: A Matcher implementation ignores its context and blocks indefinitely on a downstream call. With 4 workers, what is the effect after 4 such requests?
choices: The timeout cancels each call and the workers are freed
Shutdown returns early because the workers are blocked
The pool starts additional goroutines to compensate
All workers are stuck, so queued requests accumulate until Submit starts returning ErrQueueFull
